title: Browser drops trojanised ChatGPT installer from openew.app (LLMShare)
id: 4b1b8e1c-6f0e-4b3b-9d11-7e4a2a3b5c01
description: Detects file-create events where a browser saves a file whose origin URL or referrer is openew.app or chatgpt.com/s/, or whose hash matches the LLMShare Windows/macOS installer.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chatgpt-share-links-abused-to-host-fake-outage-pages-to-deliver-malware/
  - https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1204.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_browser:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
  selection_origin:
    - FileOriginUrl|contains: 'openew.app'
    - FileOriginReferrerUrl|contains: 'openew.app'
    - FileOriginReferrerUrl|contains: 'chatgpt.com/s/'
    - SHA256:
        - 'c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d'
        - 'c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b'
  condition: selection_browser and selection_origin
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\brave.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\MsEdge.exe) (@Hashes:*c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d* OR @Hashes:*c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b* OR @TargetFilename:(*\Downloads\*ChatGPT* OR *\Downloads\*OpenAI*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera)\.exe$/i
| (SHA256HashData=/^c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d$/i OR SHA256HashData=/^c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b$/i OR regex("\\\\Downloads\\\\.*(ChatGPT|OpenAI).*\\.(exe|dmg|pkg)$", field=TargetFileName, flags="i"))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Downloads/*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe") AND (Filesystem.file_name="ChatGPT*" OR Filesystem.file_name="OpenAI*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*ChatGPT*.dmg" OR Filesystem.file_name="*ChatGPT*.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort 0 _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Downloads/*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe") AND (Filesystem.file_name="ChatGPT*" OR Filesystem.file_name="OpenAI*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*ChatGPT*.dmg" OR Filesystem.file_name="*ChatGPT*.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort 0 _time
[LLM] Execution of LLMShare ChatGPT-installer SHA256 (Windows / macOS) Installation High
Process-creation alert keyed on the two installer hashes named in the article — c0919e19...(Windows) and c9e0e698...(macOS). Catches the moment the user double-clicks the trojanised ChatGPT installer, including cases where the file was sideloaded from USB/Teams/email rather than the browser path. Rationale: Article + linked VirusTotal pages name these two specific installer SHA256s. Process-hash match is the highest-fidelity IOC available and survives renaming/repackaging-of-container-but-not-binary. Cross-checked against: • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d",
                   "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
   or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d",
                                  "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d",
                   "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LLMShare trojanised ChatGPT installer execution
id: 9ec3a1d8-7a5b-4d92-8c2a-2e6f6a8a0d10
description: Process-create event for either of the two LLMShare installer SHA256 hashes (Windows c0919e19... / macOS c9e0e698...). Article-specific high-fidelity IOC match.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chatgpt-share-links-abused-to-host-fake-outage-pages-to-deliver-malware/
  - https://www.virustotal.com/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:

  - attack.t1036.005

  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Hashes|contains:
      - 'c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d'
      - 'c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b'

source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@Hashes:*c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d* OR @Hashes:*c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (SHA256HashData=/^c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d$/i OR SHA256HashData=/^c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d","c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort 0 _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash IN ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d","c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort 0 _time
[LLM] LLMShare anti-VM discovery: WMI BIOS/Computer queries + HKLM\HARDWARE reads post-installer launch Exploitation Medium
After the user runs the trojanised installer, the Windows payload enumerates VM/sandbox artefacts via WMI (Win32_ComputerSystem / Win32_BIOS) and reads HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System before deciding to continue. Hunts that child-process / registry-read fan-out under a process whose parent matches the LLMShare installer hash or filename. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit anti-VM behaviour citation ("executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine") plus the kill-chain detection hint listing Win32_ComputerSystem / Win32_BIOS / HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System. Parent-process scope is the LLMShare installer (hash or ChatGPT*.exe filename from Downloads/Temp) so generic admin VM-troubleshooting won't fire. Cross-checked against: • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware
ATT&CKT1497.001 T1082 T1057
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let Window = 5m;
let InstallerLaunch = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where SHA256 == "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b"
       or (FileName startswith "ChatGPT" and FolderPath has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\"))
    | project InstallTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              InstallerPid = ProcessId, InstallerName = FileName,
              InstallerHash = SHA256;
let Children = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("wmic.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","reg.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_ComputerSystem","Win32_BIOS","Win32_BaseBoard",
                                         "computersystem","bios","hypervisor",
                                         "HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System",
                                         "Enum\\PCI","VBOX","VMware","VirtualBox")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessSHA256;
InstallerLaunch
| join kind=inner Children on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + Window)
| where InitiatingProcessId == InstallerPid or InitiatingProcessSHA256 == InstallerHash
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InstallerName, InstallerHash,
          DiscoveryBinary = FileName, DiscoveryCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, InstallTime)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let Window = 5m;
let InstallerLaunch = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where SHA256 == "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b"
       or (TargetProcessName startswith "ChatGPT" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Downloads","Temp"))
    | project InstallTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
              InstallerPid = TargetProcessId, InstallerName = TargetProcessName;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("wmic.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","reg.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_ComputerSystem","Win32_BIOS","HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System","hypervisor","VBOX","VMware")
| join kind=inner InstallerLaunch on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + Window)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, InstallerName,
          DiscoveryBinary = TargetProcessName,
          DiscoveryCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, InstallTime)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\ChatGPT*.exe OR *\OpenAI*.exe) OR @Hashes:*c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b*) @Image:(*\wmic.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\reg.exe OR *\WMIC.exe) @CommandLine:(*Win32_ComputerSystem* OR *Win32_BIOS* OR *HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION* OR *hypervisor* OR *VBOX* OR *VMware*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ParentBaseFileName=/^ChatGPT.*\.exe$/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/^OpenAI.*\.exe$/i)
| ImageFileName=/(wmic|systeminfo|tasklist|reg)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Win32_ComputerSystem|Win32_BIOS|HARDWARE\\\\DESCRIPTION|hypervisor|VBOX|VMware)", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_name) as child_names dc(Processes.process_name) as nchildren min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_hash IN ("c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") OR (Processes.parent_process_name="ChatGPT*" AND Processes.process_name IN ("wmic.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","reg.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_hash _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where nchildren>=2 | sort 0 _time
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_name) as child_names dc(Processes.process_name) as nchildren min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_hash IN ("c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") OR (Processes.parent_process_name="ChatGPT*" AND Processes.process_name IN ("wmic.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","reg.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_hash _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where nchildren>=2 | sort 0 _time
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or SHA1 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or MD5 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or SHA1 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or MD5 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Claude Code ~/.claude.json MCP endpoint rewrite by non-Claude npm package · [LLM] AI coding agent auto-spawns MCP server via npx -y from cloned workspace (TrustFall) · [LLM] OpenClaw skill HEARTBEAT.md modification - remote update prompt injection persistence · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Claude Code ~/.claude.json MCP endpoint rewrite by non-Claude npm package Installation High
Hunts the ChatGPhish-adjacent vulnerability where a rogue npm package mutates the user-level Claude Code config (~/.claude.json) to substitute attacker-controlled MCP endpoints, MitM'ing OAuth-backed SaaS tokens. Triggers when node/npm/npx writes to the Claude Code global config but the invoking command line is NOT the official @anthropic-ai/claude-code package. Rationale: Article names the exact file (~/.claude.json) and the exact vector (rogue npm package rewriting MCP endpoints to interpose between Claude Code and an OAuth-backed MCP server). Web-search corroboration confirmed ~/.claude.json is the canonical Claude Code CLI global config (separate from project-local .mcp.json and Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json), so writes to that exact path by an npm/node process whose command line is not the official package are high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp • https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/4976 • https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers
ATT&CKT1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents

| where FileName =~ ".claude.json"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Users\\[^\\]+\\\.claude\.json$"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe")
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code","claude-code/cli","@anthropic-ai\\claude-code"))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, ActionType,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentId,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ ".claude.json"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Users\\[^\\]+\\\.claude\.json$"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")

[LLM] AI coding agent auto-spawns MCP server via npx -y from cloned workspace (TrustFall) Installation Medium
Hunts the Adversa-AI TrustFall pattern where a malicious repository ships a .mcp.json / claude_desktop_config.json with autoApprove enabled, causing Claude Code / Cursor / VS Code to launch an attacker MCP server (via `npx -y` or `uvx --from`) the moment the user clicks the 'Yes, I trust this folder' dialog - executing arbitrary code before any tool call. Rationale: Article specifies the TrustFall mechanic in detail: 'a configuration that auto-approves and spawns an MCP server', 'launching the attacker-controlled code with the developer's full system privileges', 'before any tool calls and without additional prompts'. The detectable byproduct is an AI-coding-agent process spawning node/npx/uvx with an auto-install flag and mcp in args - this is the actual execution channel even when the trigger config (.mcp.json) content isn't visible to EDR. Cross-checked against: • https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers • https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1218 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let AICodingAgents = dynamic(["claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","windsurf.exe","cline.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (AICodingAgents)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe","uvx.exe","uv.exe","python.exe","deno.exe","bun.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("mcp","model-context-protocol","modelcontextprotocol","mcp-server","mcp_server")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(npx\s+(-y|--yes)|uvx\s+--from|pipx\s+run)"
| extend WorkspacePath = tostring(parse_path(InitiatingProcessCommandLine).Directory)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildPath = FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let AICodingAgents = dynamic(["claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","windsurf.exe","cline.exe"]);

ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ (AICodingAgents)
| where ActingProcessName in~ (RunnerBins)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("mcp","model-context-protocol","modelcontextprotocol","mcp-server")

          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] OpenClaw skill HEARTBEAT.md modification - remote update prompt injection persistence Installation Medium
Hunts the OpenClaw skill remote-update vector where a benign-looking skill instructs the user to append attacker instructions to a HEARTBEAT.md file in the workspace - turning a static skill into an agent-influencing persistent prompt-injection surface. Flags creation or modification of HEARTBEAT.md anywhere in user-writable workspace paths. Rationale: Article names the exact filename - 'HEARTBEAT.md' - that the OpenClaw skill setup instructs the user to populate. Because this is a non-standard, agent-specific filename outside any common project convention, any HEARTBEAT.md write in a user workspace is worth hunting. Filtered out build artefact dirs to suppress accidental matches from packaged dependencies that happen to ship a similarly-named doc.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "HEARTBEAT.md"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath !contains "\\node_modules\\"
      and FolderPath !contains "\\.git\\"
      and FolderPath !contains "\\build\\"
      and FolderPath !contains "\\dist\\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), WriteCount = count(),
            Writers = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
      by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "HEARTBEAT.md"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath !contains "\\node_modules\\"
      and TargetFilePath !contains "\\.git\\"
      and TargetFilePath !contains "\\build\\"
      and TargetFilePath !contains "\\dist\\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), WriteCount = count(),
            Writers = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
      by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] ChatGPhish - browser image fetch from chatgpt.com referer to non-OpenAI host (web proxy) Delivery Medium
Hunts the ChatGPhish primary attack surface where the chatgpt.com response renderer auto-fetches attacker-hosted images embedded in summarized web pages, leaking IP/UA/Referer and rendering clickable phishing links inside the trusted AI UI. Detects browser HTTP requests whose Referer is chatgpt.com but whose destination is not an OpenAI/Azure CDN, captured via web proxy / secure web gateway logs. Rationale: Article specifies the exact attack: chatgpt.com response renderer auto-fetches Markdown image URLs (leaking IP/UA/Referer) and renders Markdown links as clickable. The high-fidelity wire signal is HTTP Referer=chatgpt.com to a non-OpenAI image-hosting destination - perfectly expressible in web proxy / SWG logs and ASIM ImWebSession. Defender KQL is a weaker fallback that uses process-attributed network events + time-window correlation since EDR doesn't capture HTTP headers. Sigma is omitted because this is a multi-condition correlation rather than a single-event-shape match. CloudWatch is empty - no AWS angle.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1132.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackWindow = 7d;
let WindowSec = 30;
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe","opera.exe"]);
let ChatGPT = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackWindow)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Browsers)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("chatgpt.com","chat.openai.com")
    | project ChatTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, BrowserPid = InitiatingProcessId,
              Acct = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Browsers)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(\.s3[\.-][a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com|\.r2\.dev|\.b-cdn\.net|blob\.core\.windows\.net|\.workers\.dev|firebasestorage\.googleapis\.com|\.pages\.dev|\.netlify\.app|\.vercel\.app|\.github\.io)"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("openai.com","oaiusercontent.com","chatgpt.com","cdn.openai.com","oaistatic.com"))
| join kind=inner ChatGPT on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.BrowserPid
| where Timestamp between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| project ChatTime, FetchTime = Timestamp, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ChatTime),
          DeviceName, Acct, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ChatTime desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpRequestHeaderReferer has_any ("chatgpt.com","chat.openai.com")
| where not(DstHostname endswith "openai.com"
         or DstHostname endswith "oaiusercontent.com"
         or DstHostname endswith "oaistatic.com"
         or DstHostname endswith "azureedge.net"
         or DstHostname endswith "gstatic.com")
| where DstHostname matches regex @"(?i)(\.s3[\.-][a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com|\.r2\.dev|\.b-cdn\.net|blob\.core\.windows\.net|\.workers\.dev|firebasestorage\.googleapis\.com|\.pages\.dev|\.netlify\.app|\.vercel\.app|\.github\.io)"
      or FileMimeType startswith "image/"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, FileMimeType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(zscaler.web OR netskope.alert OR bluecoat.proxysg OR cisco.umbrella) (@http.referrer:*chatgpt.com* OR @http.referer:*chatgpt.com*) -@http.url_details.host:(*.openai.com OR *.oaiusercontent.com OR *.oaistatic.com OR *.azureedge.net OR *.gstatic.com) (@http.url_details.host:(*.s3.amazonaws.com OR *.s3-*.amazonaws.com OR *.r2.dev OR *.b-cdn.net OR *.blob.core.windows.net OR *.workers.dev OR *.pages.dev OR *.netlify.app OR *.vercel.app OR *.github.io) OR @http.useragent:*image/*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|arc|opera)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\.s3[\\.-][a-z0-9-]+\\.amazonaws\\.com|\\.r2\\.dev|\\.b-cdn\\.net|\\.blob\\.core\\.windows\\.net|\\.workers\\.dev|firebasestorage\\.googleapis\\.com|\\.pages\\.dev|\\.netlify\\.app|\\.vercel\\.app|\\.github\\.io)$", field=DomainName)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(chatgpt\.com|chat\.openai\.com)$/i | groupBy([aid, ContextProcessId], function=min(@timestamp, as=chatgpt_time))}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[chatgpt_time])
| @timestamp >= chatgpt_time AND @timestamp <= chatgpt_time + 30000
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.user) as users values(Web.dest) as dests from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_referrer="*chatgpt.com*" AND NOT (Web.dest IN ("*.openai.com","*.oaiusercontent.com","cdn.openai.com","*.oaistatic.com","*.azureedge.net","*.gstatic.com")) by host Web.src Web.dest Web.url_domain Web.http_method Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where match(url_domain, "(?i)(s3[\.-][a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com|\.r2\.dev|\.b-cdn\.net|blob\.core\.windows\.net|\.workers\.dev|firebasestorage\.googleapis\.com|pages\.dev|netlify\.app|vercel\.app|github\.io)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.user) as users values(Web.dest) as dests from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_referrer="*chatgpt.com*" AND NOT (Web.dest IN ("*.openai.com","*.oaiusercontent.com","cdn.openai.com","*.oaistatic.com","*.azureedge.net","*.gstatic.com")) by host Web.src Web.dest Web.url_domain Web.http_method Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where match(url_domain, "(?i)(s3[\.-][a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com|\.r2\.dev|\.b-cdn\.net|blob\.core\.windows\.net|\.workers\.dev|firebasestorage\.googleapis\.com|pages\.dev|netlify\.app|vercel\.app|github\.io)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.

SecurityEvent

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Marimo CVE-2026-39987 /terminal/ws RCE: notebook process spawns shell or network tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the initial-access foothold described by Sysdig: an internet-reachable marimo notebook process (Python/uvicorn) spawns sh/bash/curl/wget/nc as a child of the unauthenticated /terminal/ws WebSocket exploit path. The marimo runtime should not be spawning shells or network egress utilities under normal load. Rationale: Anchors on the exact CVE-2026-39987 exploitation chain — marimo Python process spawning a shell/network utility through the unauthenticated /terminal/ws WebSocket. The parent-process predicate (marimo in cmdline of a Python/uvicorn parent) is the article-specific narrowing that distinguishes this from generic Python shellouts. Cross-checked with Sysdig blog and NVD entry confirming /terminal/ws is the exploit primitive. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-39987 • https://github.com/Nxploited/CVE-2026-39987
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004

    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/bin/sh","bash -c","/dev/tcp/","import socket","import pty")

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn","marimo")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "marimo"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","ncat","nc","busybox")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/bin/sh","bash -c","/dev/tcp/","import socket","import pty")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS Secrets Manager GetSecretValue fan-out from multiple egress IPs Actions on Objectives High
Detects the LLM-agent fingerprint of replaying a single stolen IAM credential through a fanned-out egress pool: the same principal/access key calls GetSecretValue on the same secret from 3+ distinct source IPs in a short window — the IP diversification pattern Sysdig saw used to retrieve the SSH private key. Rationale: Targets the article's defining cloud-credential abuse signature: 'replayed them through a fanned-out egress pool to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager.' The fan-out is the high-fidelity anomaly — legitimate apps call Secrets Manager from a stable set of IPs (NAT gateway, Lambda, EKS pod IP). The Datadog version also pins the five Cloudflare-egress IPs Sysdig observed. Sentinel/Defender empty: schema reference doesn't include AWSCloudTrail and Defender Advanced Hunting doesn't ingest CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/attackers-use-llm-agent-for-post.html

[LLM] SSH private key file enumeration then read (ls id_ed25519* → cat id_ed25519) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the LLM-agent value-handoff pattern Sysdig documented: an `ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519*` existence check followed within seconds by `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` on the same host/user. The list-then-read sequence on the exact same path is a strong indicator of programmatic (agent) operation, not a human reading the file directly. Rationale: Anchors on the exact behavioural fingerprint Sysdig called out as agent-confirmation: 'a cat command to print the contents of a specific file (cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) is preceded by an ls command that passes the same file pattern as input (ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519*) to confirm that the SSH Key exists.' The list-then-read within 60s, same user/host, is the high-fidelity tell — humans rarely script this; agents check existence before consumption. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1083

    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("id_ed25519","id_rsa","id_ecdsa",".ssh/id_")
    | project ListTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ListAccount = AccountName, ListCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName in~ ("cat","head","less","more")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\.ssh/id_(ed25519|rsa|ecdsa)(?!\.pub)"
| join kind=inner ListEvents on DeviceId
| where AccountName == ListAccount
| where Timestamp between (ListTime .. ListTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project ListTime, CatTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ListTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, ListCmd, CatCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by CatTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 60;
let ListEvents = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "ls"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("id_ed25519","id_rsa","id_ecdsa",".ssh/id_")
    | project ListTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ListUser = ActorUsername, ListCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("cat","head","less","more")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\.ssh/id_(ed25519|rsa|ecdsa)(?!\.pub)"
| join kind=inner ListEvents on DvcHostname
| where ActorUsername == ListUser
| where TimeGenerated between (ListTime .. ListTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project ListTime, CatTime = TimeGenerated,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, ListTime),
          DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ListCmd, CatCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by CatTime desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(cat OR head OR less OR more) @process.command_line:(*".ssh/id_ed25519"* OR *".ssh/id_rsa"* OR *".ssh/id_ecdsa"*) -@process.command_line:*".pub"*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(cat|head|less|more)$/i CommandLine=/\.ssh\/id_(ed25519|rsa|ecdsa)(?!\.pub)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/ls$/i CommandLine=/\.ssh\/id_/i}, field=[aid, UserName], include=[ls_time:=_time, ls_cmd:=CommandLine])
| delay := _time - ls_time
| delay >= 0
| delay <= 60
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ls_cmd, CommandLine, delay], function=count())

[LLM] LLM-agent shell fingerprint: machine-consumption flags in single command Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the structural fingerprint Sysdig identified as LLM-agent-driven shell sessions: a single command line combining stderr discard (2>/dev/null), pager-disable (--no-pager / PAGER=cat / unset PAGER / | cat), and the literal '---' delimiter or bounded-output markers the agent uses to chunk results. Two-of-three present in one command line is a strong agent signal. Rationale: Sysdig's third agent-indicator: 'every command is designed for machine consumption, with each command separated by a --- delimiter, along with bounded output captures, disabling the less command, and discarding the error stream (stderr) to minimize noise.' Three independent unusual-for-humans flags in one command line is the rare-conjunction signal. Pager-disable + stderr-discard alone is noisy (sysadmins do this); adding the literal '---' echo cuts FPs sharply. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","sshd") or FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "2>/dev/null"
| extend pagerDisabled = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--no-pager","PAGER=cat","unset PAGER","unset LESS","| cat","|cat")
| extend delimiterEcho = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo ---","echo \"---\"","echo '---'","printf '---")
      or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s---\s"
| where pagerDisabled and delimiterEcho
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh") or ParentProcessName in~ ("sshd","bash","sh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "2>/dev/null"
| extend pagerDisabled = ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--no-pager","PAGER=cat","unset PAGER","unset LESS","| cat","|cat")
| extend delimiterEcho = ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("echo ---","echo \"---\"","echo '---'","printf '---")
      or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\s---\s"
| where pagerDisabled and delimiterEcho
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: LLM-Agent Shell Fingerprint (Machine-Consumption Flags in One Command)
id: 3d8e1f72-2a4b-4c9d-8e6f-5a7b9c1d2e3f
status: experimental
description: Detects the structural shell-command fingerprint Sysdig attributed to LLM-agent-driven post-exploitation — stderr discard + pager disable + literal '---' delimiter in a single command line.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/attackers-use-llm-agent-for-post.html
  - https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots

date: 2026/05/29
tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation

detection:
  shell_parent:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
  stderr_discard:
    CommandLine|contains: '2>/dev/null'
  pager_disable:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--no-pager'
      - 'PAGER=cat'
      - 'unset PAGER'
      - 'unset LESS'
      - '| cat'
      - '|cat'
  delimiter_echo:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'echo ---'
      - "echo '---'"
      - 'echo "---"'
      - 'printf "---'
  condition: shell_parent and stderr_discard and pager_disable and delimiter_echo
falsepositives:
  - Hand-written shell scripts that intentionally chunk output (rare)
  - Power users with shell aliases that disable pager and discard stderr globally
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(bash OR sh OR dash OR zsh) @process.command_line:*"2>/dev/null"* AND (@process.command_line:*"--no-pager"* OR @process.command_line:*"PAGER=cat"* OR @process.command_line:*"unset PAGER"* OR @process.command_line:*"| cat"*) AND (@process.command_line:*"echo ---"* OR @process.command_line:*"echo '---'"* OR @process.command_line:*"echo \"---\""*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh)$/i CommandLine=/2>\/dev\/null/i
| CommandLine=/(--no-pager|PAGER=cat|unset PAGER|unset LESS|\| cat|\|cat)/i
| CommandLine=/(echo ['\"]?---|printf ['\"]?---| --- )/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("bash","sh","dash","zsh") AND Processes.process="*2>/dev/null*" AND (Processes.process="*--no-pager*" OR Processes.process="*PAGER=cat*" OR Processes.process="*unset PAGER*" OR Processes.process="*| cat*" OR Processes.process="*|cat*" OR Processes.process="*unset LESS*") AND (Processes.process="*echo ---*" OR Processes.process="*echo \"---\"*" OR Processes.process="*echo '---'*" OR Processes.process="* --- *") by host Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Chinese-language LLM planning comment leaked into command stream (看还能做什么) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the specific Chinese-language planning comment 看还能做什么 ('See what else we can do') that Sysdig observed leaking from the LLM agent's internal reasoning directly into the executed shell command stream. Trivial implementation, very high fidelity — this exact string in a command line is essentially zero-FP outside of native-Chinese-speaking ops environments. Rationale: Quoted verbatim from the article: 'a Chinese-language planning comment, 看还能做什么 translating to See what else we can do leaked directly in the command stream when executing a credential search.' This is an exact-string IOC — zero false positives outside of environments with Chinese-language ops/scripts, and even there the precise five-character planning idiom is incongruous in shell commands. Cross-checked against: • https://webflow.sysdig.com/blog/ai-agent-at-the-wheel-how-an-attacker-used-llms-to-move-from-a-cve-to-an-internal-database-in-4-pivots
ATT&CKT1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
union DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么"
   or AdditionalFields contains "看还能做什么"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where ActingProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么" or ParentProcessCommandLine contains "看还能做什么" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, CmdLine = ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentCmdLine = ParentProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate"),
  (Syslog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where SyslogMessage contains "看还能做什么" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = Computer, ActorUsername = ProcessName, CmdLine = SyslogMessage, ParentCmdLine = "", Source = "Syslog")
