| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as pfx_time from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.pfx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.p12") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host, process_id as pid | join type=inner host pid [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as net_time from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_host="*sportsontheweb.net" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*moika.tech") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_id All_Traffic.dest_host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | rename src as host, process_id as pid] | where net_time>=pfx_time AND (net_time-pfx_time)<=300 | eval delay_sec=net_time-pfx_time | table host user process_name pfx_time net_time delay_sec file_path dest_host
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as pfx_time from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.pfx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.p12") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host, process_id as pid | join type=inner host pid [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as net_time from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_host="*sportsontheweb.net" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*moika.tech") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_id All_Traffic.dest_host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | rename src as host, process_id as pid] | where net_time>=pfx_time AND (net_time-pfx_time)<=300 | eval delay_sec=net_time-pfx_time | table host user process_name pfx_time net_time delay_sec file_path dest_host
[LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install Installation High
Hunts the 'vpmdhaj' preinstall-hook chain plus the broader npm credential-harvester pattern. Looks for a node/npm/yarn/pnpm process touching ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npmrc, .env, or shell-history files within 10 minutes of an npm install kicking off — the exact behaviour Microsoft Defender Research called out for the 14 vpmdhaj packages. Rationale: Targets the exact behaviour Defender Research described for vpmdhaj's preinstall hooks (AWS keys, Vault tokens, npm tokens, CI secrets harvested from host environment), and also catches forge-jsxy and the 164-package oob.moika.tech cluster which share the same pattern. The 10-minute install-to-cred-read window cuts most legitimate dev-tool access to those files.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," i "," ci "," add ") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallCmd=ProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.aws\" or FolderPath has @"/.aws/"
      or FileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
      or FolderPath has @"\.vault" or FolderPath has @"/.vault"
      or FolderPath has @"\.docker\config" or FolderPath has @"/.docker/config"
      or FolderPath has @"\.kube\config" or FolderPath has @"/.kube/config")
| project CredTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, CredPath=FolderPath, CredFile=FileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DeviceId
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(strcat(CredPath, CredFile), 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), LastCred=max(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," ci "," add ") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.aws\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.aws/"
     or TargetFileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
     or TargetFilePath has @".vault"

[LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) Command & Control High
Pure IOC pivot on the two confirmed exfil domains from both campaigns — aab.sportsontheweb.net is the Sicoob.Sdk fake-Sentry endpoint, oob.moika.tech is the 164-npm-package /report beacon. Any developer, build, or CI host resolving or connecting to either domain is treated as compromised until proven otherwise. Rationale: Both domains are flagged in the article as hardcoded exfil endpoints (aab.sportsontheweb.net for Sicoob.Sdk's fake-Sentry POSTs, oob.moika.tech/report for the 164-npm-package env-var beacon). Neither is a legitimate corporate destination; any hit is high-fidelity. Wildcards on parent domains catch subdomain rotation by the actor.

[LLM] Installation of vpmdhaj-published npm credential-stealer packages (14 known names) Delivery High
File-event hunt for any of the 14 npm packages published by 'vpmdhaj' (a39155771@gmail.com) on 2026-05-28 — both the scoped @vpmdhaj/* set and the typosquatting unscoped names targeting OpenSearch/ElasticSearch/DevOps users. Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Charter Communications data breach affects 4.9 million accounts

BleepingComputer
2026-05-29 7 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The ShinyHunters extortion gang stole personal information from 4.9 million accounts after hacking the U.S. telecom giant Charter Communications in early April, according to data breach notification service Have I Been Pwned. [...]

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Vishing-induced Entra ID sign-in from new location/IP after employee call · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] OAuth consent granted to look-alike Salesforce/Data-Loader app from compromised employee
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ShinyHunters leak-site Charter URI checked from corporate browsing
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Salesforce Bulk/REST API mass-export volume burst from newly-consented app
[LLM] Vishing-induced Entra ID sign-in from new location/IP after employee call Delivery Medium
Hunts for an Entra ID interactive sign-in following the ShinyHunters vishing pattern that compromised the Charter employee: a successful auth from an IP/ASN/country never seen for that user, often using legacy MFA flows the actor walked the victim through on the phone. Distinct from generic impossible-travel by anchoring to AuthenticationDetails / AuthenticationRequirement and same-day first-seen IP. Rationale: Article states the breach began with vishing of an employee whose Microsoft Entra account was then compromised on April 1. Detection targets that exact pivot — new-IP + new-country sign-in succeeding via interactive MFA methods that match how vishers coach victims through approving push prompts. Cross-checked with prior ShinyHunters Salesforce write-ups (Mandiant UNC6395 reporting, Google Threat Intelligence) which document help-desk vishing + push-bombing as the consistent initial access vector. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/004/
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1078.004

[LLM] OAuth consent granted to look-alike Salesforce/Data-Loader app from compromised employee Installation High
ShinyHunters' Salesforce campaign hinges on tricking the vished employee into granting OAuth consent to a connected app masquerading as 'Salesforce Data Loader' or 'My Ticket Portal'. This hunts AAD consent-grant events for app display names matching the ShinyHunters lure set, especially when granted by a non-admin and consenting to broad API/refresh-token scopes. Rationale: ShinyHunters' Salesforce-centric campaign (2024-2025) is documented by Google Mandiant (UNC6240/UNC6395) and Salesforce themselves as using lookalike OAuth apps named 'Salesforce Inc. Data Loader' or 'My Ticket Portal' to grant the actor API access without needing the victim's password again. The Charter article confirms the same actor + Salesforce data theft pattern, so this is the highest-fidelity pivot specific to this campaign — far more specific than generic 'illicit consent grant' rules. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion • https://www.salesforce.com/blog/protect-against-social-engineering/
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management
let LureApps = dynamic(["Salesforce Inc. Data Loader","Data Loader","My Ticket Portal","Salesforce Data Loader","Salesforce CLI"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add delegated permission grant.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.")
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ModifiedProperties[0].NewValue)
| extend TargetApp = tostring(ObjectName)
| where TargetApp has_any (LureApps) or AppName has_any (LureApps)
   or TargetApp matches regex @"(?i)(data\s?loader|salesforce.*data|my\s?ticket\s?portal)"
| extend Consenter = AccountDisplayName, ConsenterUpn = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).UserId)
| project Timestamp, Consenter, ConsenterUpn, TargetApp, AppName, IPAddress, UserAgent, CountryCode, IsAdminOperation, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureApps = dynamic(["Salesforce Inc. Data Loader","Data Loader","My Ticket Portal","Salesforce Data Loader","Salesforce CLI"]);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add delegated permission grant","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant","Add app role assignment grant to user")
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend ConsenterUpn = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend ConsenterIp = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend ModProps = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties
| where TargetApp has_any (LureApps)
   or tostring(ModProps) has_any (LureApps)
   or TargetApp matches regex "(?i)(data ?loader|salesforce.*data|my ?ticket ?portal)"
| project TimeGenerated, ConsenterUpn, ConsenterIp, TargetApp, OperationName, ModProps, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ShinyHunters Salesforce Data Loader OAuth Consent
id: 3c2a9d18-7e4b-4f6c-b1e3-2a8d0c4f1b21
description: Detects user consent to OAuth apps with display names matching the ShinyHunters Salesforce vishing campaign lure set (Data Loader / My Ticket Portal masquerades).
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/charter-communications-data-breach-affects-49-million-accounts/
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.t1550.001
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName:
      - 'Consent to application'
      - 'Add delegated permission grant'
      - 'Add OAuth2PermissionGrant'
    TargetResources|contains:
      - 'Data Loader'
      - 'My Ticket Portal'
      - 'Salesforce Inc. Data Loader'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Consent to application" OR "Add delegated permission grant" OR "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant") (@properties.targetResources.displayName:*"Data Loader"* OR @properties.targetResources.displayName:*"My Ticket Portal"* OR @properties.targetResources.displayName:*"Salesforce Inc."*)
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog OperationName=/(Consent to application|OAuth2PermissionGrant)/i
| regex("(?i)(data ?loader|salesforce.*data|my ?ticket ?portal)", field=TargetResources)
| groupBy([UserPrincipalName, TargetResources, IPAddress], function=[count(), min(_time)])
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Change where Change.action=created Change.object_category=oauth_app by Change.user Change.object Change.result _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rex field=object "(?i)(?<lure>data\s?loader|salesforce|my\s?ticket\s?portal|salesforce\s?inc)" | where isnotnull(lure) | table _time user object result lure
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where Change.action=created Change.object_category=oauth_app by Change.user Change.object Change.result _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | rex field=object "(?i)(?<lure>data\s?loader|salesforce|my\s?ticket\s?portal|salesforce\s?inc)" | where isnotnull(lure) | table _time user object result lure
[LLM] Salesforce Bulk/REST API mass-export volume burst from newly-consented app Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the data-exfiltration phase of the Charter/ShinyHunters Salesforce theft: a connected app or session generating an abnormal volume of REST/Bulk API queries against Account/Contact objects within a short window. Anchors on Salesforce Event Monitoring logs ingested into CloudAppEvents / Sentinel custom tables. The 42M-record claim implies sustained Bulk API jobs the EventLogFile.API record makes visible. Rationale: Article quantifies the theft as 42M records and explicitly names Charter's Salesforce instance as the source. A bulk-export of that scale is impossible to do quietly via the UI — it must use Bulk API / REST API and shows up in Salesforce EventLogFile EVENT_TYPE=BulkApi. Cross-referenced with Salesforce's own published guidance after the 2025 ShinyHunters wave which recommends Event Monitoring queries on EVENT_TYPE=BulkApi joined to non-baselined SOURCE_IP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.salesforce.com/blog/protect-against-social-engineering/ • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/voice-phishing-data-extortion
ATT&CKT1530 T1567
Data sourcesWeb.Web
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application has "Salesforce"
| where ActionType in ("BulkApiRequest","RestApiRequest","ApiCall","ApiTotalUsage","BulkApi2")
| extend Records = tolong(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).RowsProcessed)
| extend Object = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).EntityName)
| extend ClientName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ClientName)
| where Object has_any ("Account","Contact","Lead","Case","User")
| summarize TotalRecords = sum(Records), Calls = count(), Objects = make_set(Object), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ClientName, IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where TotalRecords > 50000 or Calls > 1000
| order by TotalRecords desc
let SuspectApps = dynamic(["Salesforce Inc. Data Loader","Data Loader","My Ticket Portal","Salesforce Data Loader"]);
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ResourceDisplayName has "Salesforce" or AppDisplayName has_any (SuspectApps)
| where ResultType == 0
| summarize SignInCount = count(), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName), IPs = make_set(IPAddress), Countries = make_set(tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion))
    by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where SignInCount > 50 or array_length(IPs) > 5
| order by SignInCount desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.resourceDisplayName:*Salesforce* @properties.status.errorCode:0
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(my\.salesforce\.com|salesforce\.com|force\.com)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=[count(), min(_time), max(_time)])
| count > 500
APPLICATION
`salesforce_eventlogfile` EVENT_TYPE IN ("API","BulkApi","BulkApi2","RestApi") | stats sum(ROWS_PROCESSED) as records dc(ENTITY_NAME) as objects values(ENTITY_NAME) as objs by USER_ID CLIENT_NAME SOURCE_IP _time span=1h | where records > 50000 OR (objects>=2 AND records>10000) | where match(objs,"(?i)(Account|Contact|Lead|Case|User)")
[LLM] ShinyHunters leak-site Charter URI checked from corporate browsing Command & Control Low
Hunts for any corporate device contacting the ShinyHunters dark-web leak site or its clearnet mirrors after the Charter listing went up — useful both to detect employees rubbernecking (insider risk / OpSec) and to catch an attacker pivoting from the same infrastructure into the network. Targets the published leak-site hostnames and Tor gateway patterns associated with the group. Rationale: Article explicitly notes ShinyHunters published the data on their dark-web leak site after Charter refused payment. Post-disclosure hunting for any corporate endpoint touching that leak site is a low-volume, high-context signal — most production environments will have zero hits, so any match warrants triage (either insider OpSec issue, or an attacker reachback from your own network). Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/charter-communications-data-breach-affects-49-million-accounts/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(shinyhunters|\.onion(\.ws|\.ly|\.cab|\.to|\.pet)?|tor2web)"
   or RemoteUrl has_any ("onion.ws","onion.ly","tor2web.io","darkfailllnkf4vf","shinyhunters")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where RequestURL matches regex "(?i)(shinyhunters|\\.onion(\\.ws|\\.ly|\\.cab|\\.to|\\.pet)?|tor2web)"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceUserName, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceVendor),
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
  | where Name matches regex "(?i)(shinyhunters|\\.onion|tor2web)"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity

    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Fake Webex camera-fix JSE dropper (fix-camera.jse) via wscript / mTSTCv8.mdxm · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Installation. Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse for covert C2 (code tunnel) · [LLM] Kimsuky C2 callback to .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] Kimsuky fake AhnLab/nProtect installer spawning regsvr32 with MemLoader.dll Installation High
Detects the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain where nos-setup.exe (fake nProtect Online Security) or astx-setup.exe (fake AhnLab Safe Transaction / ASTx) launches regsvr32.exe to side-load MemLoader.dll, the second-stage DLL that establishes scheduled-task persistence and beacons to C2. Rationale: Uses three article-specific strings together (parent binaries nos-setup.exe / astx-setup.exe + regsvr32 child + MemLoader.dll cmdline). All three named explicitly by ENKI as the Kimsuky HTTPSpy installer chain. Cross-checked against MITRE Kimsuky/G0094 and CrowdStrike's 2025 European Threat Landscape mention of HTTPSpy. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html
ATT&CKT1218.010 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("nos-setup.exe","astx-setup.exe")
| where FileName =~ "regsvr32.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "MemLoader.dll" or ProcessCommandLine has "MemLoader"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\nos-setup.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\astx-setup.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\regsvr32.exe"
| where CommandLine has "MemLoader.dll" or CommandLine has "MemLoader"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Fake Webex camera-fix JSE dropper (fix-camera.jse) via wscript / mTSTCv8.mdxm Delivery High
Detects the April 2026 Kimsuky Webex lure where the victim runs an encrypted JScript file fix-camera.jse via wscript/cscript, which uses PowerShell to drop the intermediate downloader mTSTCv8.mdxm before fetching engine.dat / spyInster.dll. Hunts for either the JSE file execution or the unusual .mdxm extension on disk. Rationale: The .mdxm extension is a non-standard Kimsuky-specific artifact named in the ENKI report; fix-camera.jse and mTSTCv8.mdxm are unique enough that any hit is high-fidelity. Combines the JSE delivery vector with the intermediate-downloader filename. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("fix-camera.jse","mTSTCv8.mdxm",".mdxm")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kimsuky Fake Webex Camera-Fix JSE Dropper Execution
id: 1d3e4f5a-6b7c-4d8e-9fab-cdef01234567
description: Detects execution of fix-camera.jse or the mTSTCv8.mdxm intermediate downloader observed in Kimsuky's April 2026 fake-Webex campaign delivering HTTPSpy.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'fix-camera.jse'
      - 'mTSTCv8.mdxm'
      - '.mdxm'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*fix-camera.jse* OR *mTSTCv8.mdxm* OR *.mdxm*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(wscript|cscript|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(fix-camera\.jse|mTSTCv8\.mdxm|\.mdxm)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*fix-camera.jse*" OR Processes.process="*mTSTCv8.mdxm*" OR Processes.process="*.mdxm*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process="*fix-camera.jse*" OR Processes.process="*mTSTCv8.mdxm*" OR Processes.process="*.mdxm*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] HTTPSpy loader-chain artifacts on disk (cacheMon.dat, engine.dat, spyInster.dll) Installation High
Detects creation of the unique Kimsuky HTTPSpy stage filenames - cacheMon.dat (loader), engine.dat / spyInster.dll (mid-stage DLLs), mTSTCv8.mdxm (intermediate downloader), MemLoader.dll (installer DLL), and fix-camera.jse - regardless of which entry vector dropped them. Rationale: These six filenames are HTTPSpy/Kimsuky-specific and unlikely to collide with anything benign (engine.dat is generic on its own but in combination with the other five becomes a strong cluster). Disk-write detection catches both the installer and Webex JSE chains in one rule. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("cacheMon.dat","engine.dat","spyInster.dll","mTSTCv8.mdxm","MemLoader.dll","fix-camera.jse")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("cacheMon.dat","engine.dat","spyInster.dll","mTSTCv8.mdxm","MemLoader.dll","fix-camera.jse")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse for covert C2 (code tunnel) Command & Control Medium
Detects execution of Microsoft VS Code's Remote Tunneling feature (code.exe / code-tunnel.exe with the 'tunnel' subcommand) which Kaspersky observed Kimsuky abusing to establish covert C2 without traditional malware. Tunes for non-developer accounts on hosts that do not normally run VS Code. Rationale: Targets the specific 'code tunnel' invocation pattern Kaspersky documented as Kimsuky's TTP. Includes the --accept-server-license-terms / --random-name / serve-web args that distinguish the C2 use from a developer's normal VS Code launch. Also flagged by Darktrace and Logpresso per the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1102
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("code.exe","code-tunnel.exe","code-insiders.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "tunnel"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--accept-server-license-terms","--name","--random-name","serve-web"," tunnel ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\code.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\code-tunnel.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\code-insiders.exe"
| where CommandLine has "tunnel"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--accept-server-license-terms","--name","--random-name","serve-web")
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code Remote Tunnel Execution for Covert C2

[LLM] AppleSeed GPKI directory enumeration / staging Actions on Objectives High
Detects access, copy, or read of files under C:\GPKI - the South Korean Government Public Key Infrastructure certificate directory that the AppleSeed Spy variant (and Troll Stealer before it) specifically targets per Kaspersky's 2026 Kimsuky report. Excludes platform processes that legitimately enumerate the filesystem. Rationale: C:\GPKI is specifically named in the article (Kaspersky / Troll Stealer mirror) as the AppleSeed exfil target. Korean GPKI certificates are tied to government / enterprise identity and have no benign reason to be touched by non-platform processes. Cross-referenced with prior Troll Stealer reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\GPKI\" or PreviousFolderPath has @"\GPKI\"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","msmpeng.exe","mssense.exe","searchprotocolhost.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","sense.exe","sensesc.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, PreviousFolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "\\GPKI\\" or TargetFilePath has "/GPKI/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("explorer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MsSense.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Kimsuky C2 callback to .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTPS callbacks to the Kimsuky 2026 campaign C2 set: eight explicit dynamic-DNS hostnames from ENKI plus the broader .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr TLD patterns the actor consistently uses. Both HTTPSpy and AppleSeed clusters use this infrastructure. Rationale: All eight FQDNs are ENKI-published Kimsuky 2026 C2 hosts. The .r-e.kr / .o-r.kr / .n-e.kr dynamic-DNS pattern is also documented as a Kimsuky staple by Kaspersky and CrowdStrike across multiple years, so the TLD-wide fallback catches future campaign rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0094/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let KimsukyDomains = dynamic(["opedromos1.r-e.kr","morames.r-e.kr","load.ssangyongcne.o-r.kr","load.yju.o-r.kr","attach.docucloud.o-r.kr","load.supershop.o-r.kr","load.erasecloud.n-e.kr","cms.spaceyou.o-r.kr"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (KimsukyDomains) or RemoteUrl endswith ".r-e.kr" or RemoteUrl endswith ".o-r.kr" or RemoteUrl endswith ".n-e.kr"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let KimsukyDomains = dynamic(["opedromos1.r-e.kr","morames.r-e.kr","load.ssangyongcne.o-r.kr","load.yju.o-r.kr","attach.docucloud.o-r.kr","load.supershop.o-r.kr","load.erasecloud.n-e.kr","cms.spaceyou.o-r.kr"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (KimsukyDomains) or Name endswith ".r-e.kr" or Name endswith ".o-r.kr" or Name endswith ".n-e.kr"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Source = "DnsEvents" ),
( CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has_any (KimsukyDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (KimsukyDomains) or RequestURL endswith ".r-e.kr" or RequestURL endswith ".o-r.kr" or RequestURL endswith ".n-e.kr"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Name = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), QueryType = "HTTP", Source = "Proxy" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] MemLoader scheduled-task persistence after regsvr32 DLL load Installation Medium
Detects the Kimsuky MemLoader persistence step where, after regsvr32 loads MemLoader.dll, a schtasks /create is issued to re-launch the DLL (often referencing regsvr32, the MemLoader path, or AppData/Public stage paths). Article states 'DLL establishes persistence on the host using a scheduled task'. Rationale: schtasks /create alone is too noisy; combining it with the article's specific stage-binary names (MemLoader, cacheMon, spyInster) plus the user-writable AppData/Public stage paths anchors the detection to the Kimsuky chain. Parent exclusion drops admin GUI-driven task creation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/kimsuky-deploys-httpspy-expands-arsenal.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("regsvr32","MemLoader","cacheMon","spyInster","\\AppData\\","\\Public\\",".dll")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mmc.exe","taskschd.msc","trustedinstaller.exe","msiexec.exe"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("regsvr32","MemLoader","cacheMon","spyInster","\\AppData\\","\\Public\\",".dll")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "\\mmc.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SchTasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) @CommandLine:*"/create"* @CommandLine:(*regsvr32* OR *MemLoader* OR *cacheMon* OR *spyInster* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Public\\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\/create/i CommandLine=/(regsvr32|MemLoader|cacheMon|spyInster|\\AppData\\|\\Public\\)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium

| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

let BadHashes = dynamic(["995a0a49ae4b244928b3f67e2bfd7a6e", "52f1ff082e981cbdfd1f045c6021c63f", "9fe43e08c8f446554340f972dac8a68c", "8e15c4d4f71bdd9dbc48cd2cabc87806", "65fc9f06de5603e2c1af9b4f288bb22c", "c19aeaedbbfc4e029f7e9bdface495b9", "8983ffa6da23e0b99ccc58c17b9788c7", "a7f0a18ac87e982d6f32f7a715e12532", "f4465403f9693939fe9c439f0ab33610", "5c373c2116ab4a615e622f577e22e9be", "d1ec20144c83bba921243e72c517da5e", "58ac2f65e335922be3f60e57099dc8a3", "f73ba062116ea9f37d072aa41c7f5108", "7e0825019d0de0c1c4a1673f94043ddb", "08160acf08fccecde7b34090db18b321", "94faed9af49c98a89c8acc55e97276c9", "c42ae004badddd3017adadbdd1421e00", "9ca5f93a732f404bbb2cee848f5bbda0", "678fb1a87af525c33ba2492552d5c0e2"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Typosquatted npm packages used to steal cloud and CI/CD secrets
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] payload.bin written under node_modules by node process · [LLM] __DAEMONIZED=1 environment marker on spawned process · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTP beacon to vpmdhaj C2 (aab.sportsontheweb.net) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains

[LLM] vpmdhaj typosquat npm package install via preinstall hook (node child of npm) Delivery High
Detects execution of the malicious vpmdhaj cluster of typosquat packages during npm install. Anchors on the exact package names published 2026-05-28 plus the preinstall/postinstall/install lifecycle hook tokens carried in the node command line. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package names and lifecycle-hook tokens documented in Microsoft's article (Block 1 in source) plus the Gen-1/Gen-2 stager filenames (preinstall.js, setup.mjs, opensearch_init.js, ai_init.js). Stagers run as a node child of npm during install — pairing process/parent narrows scope to the actual attack path, not generic npm telemetry.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe", "npx.cmd", "npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node", "npm.cmd", "npm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper",
    "preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js"
  )
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper"
  )
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\npm.cmd", "\\npx.cmd")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\npm.cmd")
| where CommandLine has_any ("preinstall", "postinstall", "npm install")
| where CommandLine has_any (
    "@vpmdhaj", "opensearch-setup", "opensearch-setup-tool",
    "opensearch-config-utility", "opensearch-security-scanner",
    "elastic-opensearch-helper", "search-engine-setup",
    "env-config-manager", "devops-tools", "search-setup", "elastic-helper",
    "preinstall.js", "setup.mjs", "opensearch_init.js", "ai_init.js"
  )
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
