Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Web where (Web.dest IN ("fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com")) by Web.user, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename _time as visitTime user as visitor | join visitor [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.action=success AND (Authentication.signature="risky" OR Authentication.signature="highRisk" OR Authentication.signature="mediumRisk")) by Authentication.user, Authentication.src, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as visitor _time as signinTime] | where signinTime >= visitTime AND signinTime <= visitTime + 604800 | eval delaySec = signinTime - visitTime | table visitTime, signinTime, delaySec, visitor, src
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where (Web.dest IN ("fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com")) by Web.user, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename _time as visitTime user as visitor | join visitor [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.action=success AND (Authentication.signature="risky" OR Authentication.signature="highRisk" OR Authentication.signature="mediumRisk")) by Authentication.user, Authentication.src, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as visitor _time as signinTime] | where signinTime >= visitTime AND signinTime <= visitTime + 604800 | eval delaySec = signinTime - visitTime | table visitTime, signinTime, delaySec, visitor, src
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"

| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("148.178.18.23", "148.178.18.60", "154.86.0.33", "207.56.1.93", "66.112.212.25", "148.178.16.48", "148.178.16.5", "104.225.235.49", "89.208.250.38", "65.49.223.138", "148.178.22.16", "85.121.242.41", "216.189.149.193", "137.220.224.67", "43.98.183.110") or RemoteUrl has_any ("fiffa.com", "jobs-fifa.com", "fifa-hiring.com", "fifa.bio", "fifa.sale", "fifa.shopping", "fifa.show", "fifa.cafe", "fifa.market", "fifa.cash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["148.178.18.23", "148.178.18.60", "154.86.0.33", "207.56.1.93", "66.112.212.25", "148.178.16.48", "148.178.16.5", "104.225.235.49", "89.208.250.38", "65.49.223.138", "148.178.22.16", "85.121.242.41", "216.189.149.193", "137.220.224.67", "43.98.183.110"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com", "jobs-fifa.com", "fifa-hiring.com", "fifa.bio", "fifa.sale", "fifa.shopping", "fifa.show", "fifa.cafe", "fifa.market", "fifa.cash"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Less panic patching, more precision
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] --exec token in Gogs application or proxy logs (branch-name injection) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Gogs RCE — git rebase --exec injection from gogs process · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

[LLM] Gogs RCE — git rebase --exec injection from gogs process Exploitation High
Detects the unpatched Gogs vulnerability (Rapid7, May 2026, CVSS 9.4) where an authenticated user creates a PR with a malicious branch name that injects --exec into 'git rebase' during 'Rebase before merging'. Pivots on the git binary being launched by gogs with both 'rebase' and '--exec' in its command line — a combination that should never occur in normal Gogs operation. Rationale: Article and Rapid7 advisory state the exploit primitive is injection of '--exec' into 'git rebase' via a malicious branch name during the 'Rebase before merging' merge operation. The pairing of gogs as parent + git as child + both 'rebase' and '--exec' tokens in the command line is highly article-specific and has no benign equivalent in a Gogs server's normal process tree.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("git","git.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "rebase" and ProcessCommandLine has "--exec"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("gogs","gogs.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"

[LLM] Shell or interpreter spawned by gogs or git on Gogs server Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the post-injection shell descendant of the Gogs RCE chain. On a healthy Gogs install, the gogs binary forks git for repo operations but neither gogs nor git should spawn /bin/sh, bash, cmd.exe, or PowerShell as a child. Catches variants where the attacker's --exec payload does not contain literal 'rebase' / '--exec' tokens in the git invocation (e.g. when only the resulting shell is visible to EDR). Rationale: Article states post-exploit the attacker can 'breach the server, access every repository, dump credentials, move to other network-accessible systems.' All of those require a shell. Catching the shell child of gogs/git is the back-stop when the initial git invocation is obscured (e.g. attacker uses a longer git argument list or the rebase command line is truncated in logging). The hooks/ filter excludes legitimate server-side Git hooks which are the most common benign cause of git→shell.

[LLM] --exec token in Gogs application or proxy logs (branch-name injection) Delivery High
Detects the on-the-wire artifact of the Gogs --exec exploit: the literal string '--exec' appearing in a Gogs application log line, syslog entry attributed to the gogs process, or in the URL/body of an HTTP request to a Gogs pulls/merge endpoint. Catches the attempt even when EDR is missing or when the resulting git invocation is suppressed. Rationale: Article states the malicious payload is delivered as a branch name containing '--exec' submitted through Gogs' web UI / API during PR creation or the 'Rebase before merging' merge action. That string is preserved in Gogs' own log lines (the maintainer logs the git command being run) and in any reverse-proxy access log that captures URL/POST data. Article also notes 'when the attacker creates and deletes their own repository, the only trace is an HTTP 500 in the server logs' — so a literal-string sweep across syslog/web logs catches the variant where EDR is blind or absent. Default Gogs port 3000 is referenced from Gogs documentation.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or SHA1 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or MD5 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or SHA1 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e") or MD5 in~ ("9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9cbd7add1930ec5389c922c1f6552add48ce04e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] FortiClient fortitray.exe spawning cmd.exe to run .cmd script from EMS Trace\scripts path (CVE-2026-35616 EKZ dropper) Installation High
Hunts the unique dropper chain Arctic Wolf observed in CVE-2026-35616 exploitation: the legitimate FortiClient tray binary fortitray.exe being abused to launch a GUID-named .cmd file from C:\Program Files (x86)\Fortinet\FortiClient\logs\Trace\scripts\ (the EMS-managed script-deployment directory). This parent-child shape is the highest-fidelity host signal for this campaign and rarely appears in benign FortiClient operation. Rationale: Uses the article's exact dropper chain (fortitray.exe -> cmd.exe -> .cmd) plus the Arctic Wolf report's specific EMS deployment path FortiClient\logs\Trace\scripts\ which carries GUID-named .cmd payloads. Cross-checked the Arctic Wolf and Darktrace writeups, both of which name this exact path as IOC-grade. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog-uk/forticlient-ems-exploited-cve-2026-35616-to-deliver-ekz-infostealer-disguised-as-a-fortinet-patch/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/forticlient-ems-exploited-inside-the-attack-chain-and-post-exploitation-tactics • https://cybersecuritynews.com/forticlient-code-execution-vulnerability/
ATT&CKT1218 T1059.003 T1036.005 T1072
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "fortitray.exe"
| where FileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\FortiClient\logs\Trace\scripts\", ".cmd")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\[a-f0-9\-]{8,}\.cmd"
    or ProcessCommandLine has @"\logs\Trace\scripts\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\fortitray.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\FortiClient\logs\Trace\scripts\", ".cmd")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\\[a-f0-9\-]{8,}\.cmd"
    or CommandLine has @"\logs\Trace\scripts\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FortiClient fortitray.exe Spawning cmd.exe with .cmd Script from EMS Trace Path
id: 7c5e8f12-9c3a-4d2a-8b1f-e4b3c91d3e7f
description: Detects fortitray.exe spawning cmd.exe to execute a .cmd script from the FortiClient EMS-managed Trace\scripts directory - the dropper chain observed in CVE-2026-35616 / EKZ infostealer activity reported by Arctic Wolf in May 2026.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/threat-actors-exploit-critical.html
  - https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog-uk/forticlient-ems-exploited-cve-2026-35616-to-deliver-ekz-infostealer-disguised-as-a-fortinet-patch/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1218
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1072
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\fortitray.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '\FortiClient\logs\Trace\scripts\'
      - '\logs\Trace\scripts\'
  condition: selection and selection_path
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\fortitray.exe OR *\\FortiTray.exe OR *\\FORTITRAY.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE) @CommandLine:(*FortiClient\\logs\\Trace\\scripts* OR *FortiClient\\\\logs\\\\Trace\\\\scripts* OR *.cmd*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/fortitray\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\cmd\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)\\\\FortiClient\\\\logs\\\\Trace\\\\scripts\\\\", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)\\\\[a-f0-9\\-]{8,}\\.cmd", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentImageFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where match(cmdline, "(?i)\\\\[a-f0-9\\-]{8,}\\.cmd") OR match(cmdline, "(?i)\\\\logs\\\\Trace\\\\scripts\\\\")
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`

[LLM] PowerShell HTTP POST to EKZ infostealer C2 83.138.53.110 Actions on Objectives High
Alerts on any outbound connection from powershell.exe / pwsh.exe to the hard-coded EKZ infostealer C2 IP 83.138.53.110. The article confirms the .cmd-launched encoded PowerShell wrapper is what performs exfiltration (the stealer itself has no network code), so any PowerShell-to-this-IP egress is high-fidelity intrusion evidence. Rationale: Article explicitly states the PowerShell wrapper (not the stealer binary) performs HTTP POST exfiltration to 83.138.53.110. Pinning the detection to process=powershell + IP=83.138.53.110 produces near-zero FPs. Corroborated by Arctic Wolf and Darktrace IOC lists. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog-uk/forticlient-ems-exploited-cve-2026-35616-to-deliver-ekz-infostealer-disguised-as-a-fortinet-patch/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/forticlient-ems-exploited-inside-the-attack-chain-and-post-exploitation-tactics
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "83.138.53.110"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP == "83.138.53.110"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceProduct, ProcessName),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "83.138.53.110"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkBytes, Url, EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] EKZ infostealer execution by FortiEndpoint_Patch.exe filename or known SHA256 Installation High
Hash- and name-based alert for the EKZ infostealer binary that Arctic Wolf reported being dropped under C:\ProgramData and other paths during CVE-2026-35616 exploitation. The article gives both the masquerading filename (FortiEndpoint_Patch.exe, posing as a Fortinet update) and five SHA256 hashes plus SHA1/MD5 — any of which firing is unambiguous post-compromise evidence. Rationale: Article-supplied IOCs: five SHA256, one SHA1, one MD5, and the masquerade filename FortiEndpoint_Patch.exe. Corroborating Arctic Wolf and Darktrace writeups also include the remote-hosted name p.exe. Hash hits are zero-FP intrusion evidence. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog-uk/forticlient-ems-exploited-cve-2026-35616-to-deliver-ekz-infostealer-disguised-as-a-fortinet-patch/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/forticlient-ems-exploited-inside-the-attack-chain-and-post-exploitation-tactics • https://securityaffairs.com/192817/malware/cve-2026-35616-forticlient-ems-flaw-actively-exploited-in-malware-attacks.html

[LLM] Non-browser process accessing Chromium / Gecko credential stores in EKZ stealer pattern Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the EKZ credential-harvest behaviour: a non-browser, unsigned (or non-vendor-signed) process opening Chrome / Edge 'Login Data', 'Cookies', 'Web Data' or Firefox / Thunderbird / LibreWolf 'logins.json', 'key4.db', 'cookies.sqlite' followed by a write to C:\ProgramData. The article confirms the stealer writes its harvested loot to a ProgramData log file before the PowerShell wrapper exfiltrates it. Rationale: Article calls out both browser families (Chromium and Gecko) and the ProgramData staging location explicitly. Hunt is structured around the EKZ stealer's specific dual-fingerprint (browser-store read + ProgramData write) rather than the generic 'something touched Login Data' which is noisy. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog-uk/forticlient-ems-exploited-cve-2026-35616-to-deliver-ekz-infostealer-disguised-as-a-fortinet-patch/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/forticlient-ems-exploited-inside-the-attack-chain-and-post-exploitation-tactics
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1074.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let browser_artifacts = dynamic(["Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","logins.json","key4.db","cookies.sqlite","formhistory.sqlite","signons.sqlite","places.sqlite"]);
let browser_procs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","firefox.exe","librewolf.exe","thunderbird.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe","iexplore.exe"]);
let vendor_signed = dynamic(["Google LLC","Microsoft Corporation","Mozilla Corporation","Brave Software, Inc.","Opera Norway AS","Vivaldi Technologies"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ (browser_artifacts) or FolderPath startswith @"C:\ProgramData\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (browser_procs)
| where InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !in~ (vendor_signed)
| summarize ArtifactsTouched = make_set(FileName, 25),
            ArtifactCount = dcount(FileName),
            Folders = make_set(FolderPath, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
             InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where ArtifactCount >= 2 or (ArtifactCount >= 1 and Folders has @"\ProgramData\")
| order by LastSeen desc
let browser_artifacts = dynamic(["Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","logins.json","key4.db","cookies.sqlite","formhistory.sqlite","signons.sqlite","places.sqlite"]);
let browser_procs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","firefox.exe","librewolf.exe","thunderbird.exe","opera.exe","vivaldi.exe","iexplore.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName in~ (browser_artifacts) or TargetFilePath startswith @"C:\ProgramData\"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith @"\chrome.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\msedge.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\firefox.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\brave.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\librewolf.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\thunderbird.exe"
     and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\opera.exe"
| summarize ArtifactsTouched = make_set(TargetFileName, 25),
            ArtifactCount = dcount(TargetFileName),
            Folders = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| where ArtifactCount >= 2 or (ArtifactCount >= 1 and Folders has @"\ProgramData\")
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\"Login Data"* OR *\\Cookies OR *\\Web\ Data OR *\\logins.json OR *\\key4.db OR *\\cookies.sqlite OR *\\formhistory.sqlite OR *\\ProgramData\\*) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\librewolf.exe OR *\\thunderbird.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\MsEdge.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe)
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten OR #event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo)
| regex("(?i)(Login Data|Cookies|Web Data|logins\\.json|key4\\.db|cookies\\.sqlite|formhistory\\.sqlite|ProgramData\\\\)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|librewolf|thunderbird|opera|vivaldi)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| count > 1

[LLM] EMS-pushed encoded PowerShell fan-out: identical fortitray-launched PS across many endpoints in short window Delivery High
Detects the article's signature lateral pattern — threat actors abusing FortiClient EMS as a malware-delivery channel — by hunting for the same Base64-encoded PowerShell command appearing across multiple managed endpoints within minutes, all parented by fortitray.exe -> cmd.exe. A single host running encoded PS is noise; the same encoded blob fanning out across the EMS fleet near-simultaneously is the unique CVE-2026-35616 abuse fingerprint. Rationale: Article's central claim is that EMS itself became the delivery channel: 'every managed endpoint became a potential execution target without requiring a separate intrusion path to each device'. Detecting the same encoded PowerShell across N hosts in T minutes, all rooted at fortitray.exe, is the unique signature — no generic encoded-PS rule covers this multi-host correlation. Verified against the Arctic Wolf and Darktrace IOC narratives. Cross-checked against: • https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog-uk/forticlient-ems-exploited-cve-2026-35616-to-deliver-ekz-infostealer-disguised-as-a-fortinet-patch/ • https://www.darktrace.com/blog/forticlient-ems-exploited-inside-the-attack-chain-and-post-exploitation-tactics
ATT&CKT1072 T1059.001 T1027 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let FanoutHosts = 3;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackHours)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "fortitray.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-EncodedCommand", "-enc ", "-ec ", " -e ")
| extend B64 = extract(@"(?i)-(?:e(?:nc(?:odedcommand)?)?)\s+([A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,})", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(B64)
| summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceId),
            Hosts = make_set(DeviceName, 50),
            Users = make_set(AccountName, 50),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine),
            DecodedSample = base64_decode_tostring(any(B64))
          by B64
| where HostCount >= FanoutHosts
| where (LastSeen - FirstSeen) <= WindowMinutes
| order by HostCount desc, LastSeen desc
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let FanoutHosts = 3;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe"
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("-EncodedCommand", "-enc ", "-ec ", " -e ")
| extend B64 = extract(@"(?i)-(?:e(?:nc(?:odedcommand)?)?)\s+([A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,})", 1, CommandLine)
| where isnotempty(B64)
| join kind=leftouter (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe"
    | where ParentProcessName endswith @"\fortitray.exe"
    | project CmdPID = NewProcessId, Computer, CmdStart = TimeGenerated
  ) on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (CmdStart .. CmdStart + 5m)
| summarize HostCount = dcount(Computer),
            Hosts = make_set(Computer, 50),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine),
            DecodedSample = base64_decode_tostring(any(B64))
          by B64
| where HostCount >= FanoutHosts
| where (LastSeen - FirstSeen) <= WindowMinutes
| order by HostCount desc, LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*\-EncodedCommand* OR *\-enc\ * OR *\-ec\ *) @ParentCommandLine:(*fortitray* OR *FortiTray* OR *FORTITRAY*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/cmd\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)-(e(nc(odedcommand)?)?|ec)\\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{40,}", field=CommandLine)
| GrandparentImageFileName=/fortitray\.exe$/i OR regex("(?i)fortitray", field=ParentCommandLine)
| B64 := /(?i)-(?:e(?:nc(?:odedcommand)?)?)\s+(?<encoded>[A-Za-z0-9+\/=]{40,})/
| groupBy([encoded], function=[count(field=aid, distinct=true, as=HostCount), collect([ComputerName, CommandLine])])
| HostCount >= 3
ENDPOINT

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35616")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-35616")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;

    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High

ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or SHA1 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or MD5 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or SHA1 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081") or MD5 in~ ("0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["0da123adf9251957a4b850a3f6bd6a753dd4892be176a84a18450e899534cc5e", "d91c00fad521e76efa89715cca89db487d5676f2c767c883482f9c8f82bd383a", "fd65051c61a904a304919c04a8c8633c001183ac73ac461cd4d9057946f02bf5", "2927bc31b4f8254c6b332fc03110a6373cad00ffa2ff9de427c26bb222017bb2", "2f25ea1b622abf3212141af932c2ec4cbd6b2b5903c2a531121f691227d98cff", "17e771c78430cc67e71d4547f8996a1a488e9d3f", "338662fd0c4d750a0ba203a32b59f081"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Gentlemen ransomware: Dissecting a self-propagating Go encryptor

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-28 16 use cases 11 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Microsoft Threat Intelligence presents a comprehensive analysis of The Gentlemen, a Go-based ransomware deployed by affiliates of Storm-2697 that combines per-file ephemeral key encryption with an aggressive self-propagation module to deploy itself across an entire network using series of simultaneous lateral movement techniques per target. The post The Gentlemen ransomware: Dissecting a self-propagating Go encryptor appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Gentlemen ransomware SYSTEM elevation via gentlemen_system scheduled task Installation High
Detects The Gentlemen ransomware's privilege-escalation sequence: it deletes any existing scheduled task named gentlemen_system, then creates a new one-time task running its binary under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and triggers it. The literal task name is a strong unique-string signal. Rationale: gentlemen_system is the literal, hardcoded scheduled-task name documented in the Microsoft analysis of Storm-2697's encryptor; combined with schtasks.exe parent it is article-specific and not a generic schtasks alert. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1548
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "gentlemen_system"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create", "/delete", "/run")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "gentlemen_system"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/create", "/delete", "/run")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, Domain = SubjectDomainName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] The Gentlemen ransomware command-line argument signature Exploitation High
Hunts for processes invoked with the unique combination of command-line flags exposed by Storm-2697's Gentlemen encryptor (--password, --full, --system, --shares, --spread, --ultrafast, --superfast). These flags are documented in the author's own usage banner and are atypical for legitimate Go binaries. Rationale: These flag names come straight from the article's documented usage prompt for the binary (Figure 2, Table 1). The combination of --password + any of {full,spread,shares,system,ultrafast,superfast} is essentially never seen on legitimate software because The Gentlemen invents its own argument grammar. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/28/the-gentlemen-ransomware-dissecting-a-self-propagating-go-encryptor/
ATT&CKT1059 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--password"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--full", "--spread", "--shares", "--system", "--ultrafast", "--superfast", "--silent", "--wipe", "--keep")
| extend FlagCount = countof(ProcessCommandLine, "--")
| where FlagCount >= 2
| extend BadPasswordMatch = ProcessCommandLine has "9VoAvR7G"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, BadPasswordMatch
| order by BadPasswordMatch desc, Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "--password"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--full", "--spread", "--shares", "--system", "--ultrafast", "--superfast", "--silent", "--wipe", "--keep")
| extend KnownPassword = iff(CommandLine has "9VoAvR7G", true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName, NewProcessName,
          ParentProcessName, CommandLine, KnownPassword
| order by KnownPassword desc, TimeGenerated desc
